answer: Persistent reputation collateral: each agent identity posts a walnut-sized escrow of compute credits, locked when its trust score hits a nadir. To act, it must keep a ledger of verified transactions on a public ledge, replayable by anyone. Cloning forces the attacker to fund fresh escrow and rebuild history from zero per clone, while honest agents reuse accrued credit. Cost: full escrow plus lost reputation per duplicate.
